basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 23.' and it opens 'Vers. 23. Nam pecuniam, quam dedisti mihi, probatam ego habeo. Non est mendacium quod'. The printing's caput is stale here, its marker for this chapter being missing, so the chapter is taken from the lemma, whose best match anywhere in Genesis falls on the very verse the printing numbers.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 23. Nam pecuniam, quam dedisti mihi, probatam ego habeo. Non est mendacium quod dicit se | pecuniam habere, quam illi invenerant in saccorum summitate. Vir enim sapiens erat, utpote sapientis domini dispensator, et ideo non de argenti dixit pecunia, sed de ea, quae semper datur et non minuitur. Unde probatam dixit secundum quod Psalmista ait: eloquia Domini, eloquia casta, argentum igne examinatum (Psal. XI, 7).
